p: בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא בְּסֻכּוֹת (פְּסִיקְתָּא דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא כז, א)
In the Pesikta on Sukkos (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana 27:1)
וּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (אֱמוֹר פָּרָשָׁה ל; וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל, א)
and the Midrash Rabbah (Emor, parashah 30; Vayikra Rabbah 30:1):
"And you shall take for yourselves," etc. (Vayikra 23:40).
קְחוּ מוּסָרִי וְאַל כָּסֶף (מִשְׁלֵי ח, י),
קְחוּ מוּסָרָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וְאַל כָּסֶף.
take the instruction of the Torah and not silver.
לָמָּה תִשְׁקְלוּ כֶסֶף בְּלֹא לֶחֶם (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, ב),
"Why do you weigh out silver for that which is not bread?" (Yeshayahu 55:2) —
לָמָּה אַתֶּם שׁוֹקְלִים כֶּסֶף לִבְנֵי שֵׂעִיר?
why do you weigh out silver to the sons of Seir?
"For that which is not bread" — because you were not sated
"And your toil for that which does not satisfy" —
while the nations of the world are sated?
"For that which does not satisfy" — because you were not sated
דִּכְתִיב וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי (מִשְׁלֵי ט, ה).
as it is written, "And drink of the wine that I have mixed" (Mishlei 9:5).
The reason he opened with this
"Hear, my son, the instruction of your father,
and do not forsake the teaching of your mother."
"The instruction of your father" is the Written Torah,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת לה, ב):
in keeping with what they said in the Gemara (Berachos 35b):
וְאֵין אָבִיךָ אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
"'Your father' is none other than the Holy One, Blessed is He,
and 'your mother' is none other than Knesses Yisrael."
"The teaching of your mother" is the Oral Torah.
The Written Torah is called "the instruction of your father"
because it is what is heard by implication, the "no" from the "yes,"
for one who transgresses, Heaven forbid;
כַּאֲשֶׁר יְיַסֵּר אִישׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ (דְּבָרִים ח, ה),
who raises the rod to frighten him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּזוֹהַר חָדָשׁ כִּי תָבוֹא עג, ב)
as they said (Zohar Chadash, Ki Savo 73b),
that he lets out a great roar, etc.,
so that the fear will suffice,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (צְפַנְיָה ג, ז)
along the lines of what is said (Tzefanyah 3:7),
"Surely you will fear Me, you will accept instruction."
"You will make known to me the path of life,"
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (שָׁם; וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל, ב):
and in the Midrash Rabbah (ibid.; Vayikra Rabbah 30:2):
to the life of the World to Come," etc.;
This is the fear from the father's instruction
that is in the Written Torah,
in that he lets out a great roar.
And the end of the verse,
"Pleasant things are at Your right hand forever,"
is expounded as referring to the lulav:
The one holding the palm branch in his hand.
Also, the connection of the opening
to the word "And you shall take":
for it is brought in the Midrash Rabbah (ibid. 30:1),
that is, as we find with Rabban Gamliel,
who bought it for a thousand zuz,
This is why he opened with the verse "Take My instruction":
which is the fulfillment of the six hundred and thirteen mitzvos.
And it is brought in the holy Zohar
"Striving after the Holy One, Blessed is He,
but striving for the Holy One, Blessed is He,
This is what is said: "Take My instruction" —
And this is what is said: "And you shall take for yourselves," etc. —
Afterwards he brings the verse from Yeshayahu,
לָמָּה תִשְׁקְלוּ כֶסֶף בְּלֹא לֶחֶם וְגוֹמֵר,
"Why do you weigh out silver for that which is not bread," etc.,
and he expounded "bread" as the words of Torah.
And it is brought (Ra'aya Mehemna, beginning of Parashas Eikev,
and drink of the wine that I have mixed' —
the bread of the Written Torah
and the wine of the Oral Torah."
And he expounded "for that which does not satisfy"
as referring to the wine of Torah;
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
this follows what they said in the Gemara
(Berachos 49b): "'And you will be sated' — this is drinking."
אַךְ לָמָּה נִדְרָשׁ שְׂבִיעָה עַל שְׁתִיָּה?
But why is satiety expounded as drinking?
It is in keeping with what was said,
that bread is the Written Torah
and wine is the Oral Torah.
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah," etc.,
כִּי בְּרוֹב חָכְמָה רוֹב כָּעַס (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח),
"for in much wisdom is much anger" (Koheles 1:18):
for the Written Torah would have sufficed.
when the yetzer hara grows stronger every day,
that is, that the holiness should remain permanently
and he be saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara.
And this is the meaning of satiety:
that the satiety from the bread should remain
וְזֶה עִנְיַן שֶׁנִּמְשַׁל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And this is why the Oral Torah is likened
that the words of Torah are likened
which is expounded (there) as referring to a student;
that is, in the Oral Torah,
for the Written Torah is "wrapped up and set down,"
and no teacher is needed for it:
And this is what they said (Taanis 9a):
"The well was in the merit of Miriam";
as they said (in the Mechilta, Yisro),
וְזֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this alludes to the Oral Torah
And it is brought in the Gemara (Sotah 11b):
and King David, peace be upon him,
was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus —
מַלְכוּת פֶּה, תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
"Malchus is the mouth; we call it the Oral Torah"
And this is what they said: "of the wine that I have mixed" —
the wine of the Oral Torah,
so that he will not hunger;
that is, that the yetzer hara will not overpower him.
And this is what they said: "'And you will be sated' — this is drinking."
וְדָרַשׁ כָּאן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
And here he expounded according to what they said
"Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah —
and the yoke of earning a living are removed from him," etc.
That is: one who accepts upon himself
the yoke of the Written Torah —
the yoke of government is removed from him.
And this is how he expounded "Why do you weigh out silver"
to the nations of the world "for that which is not bread":
because you were not sated with the bread of Torah,
"Of My bread" — the bread of the Written Torah;
וְלֶחֶם לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ יִסְעָד (תְּהִלִּים קד, טו)
and "bread sustains the heart of man" (Tehillim 104:15)
אַךְ יִצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם עוֹד מִתְגַּבֵּר,
but a person's yetzer still grows stronger,
and much wisdom is needed to be saved from it,
that is, that there be satiety.
And about this it is said (ibid.),
"And wine gladdens the heart of man";
וְהוּא לְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא):
and this is "gladness for the upright of heart" (Tehillim 97:11):
to empty the evil out of the heart of the fool.
no toil would have been needed,
the fruit of the trees of the Garden;
even wheat was a kind of tree,
and it would grow loaves, etc.,
as it will be in the future,
But after the corruption he was cursed:
בְּזֵעַת אַפֶּךָ תֹּאכַל לֶחֶם (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג, יט),
"By the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread" (Bereishis 3:19),
and "how many toils Adam HaRishon toiled
until he found bread to eat," etc.,
And one who accepts upon himself
the yoke of the Oral Torah,
with little sleep and little pleasure,
as they said in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Noach 3)
שֶׁעַל זֶה הָיָה הַכְפָּיַית הַר כְּגִיגִית,
that it was over this that the mountain was held over them like a barrel,
whereas the Written Torah they accepted with love
and said, "We will do and we will hear" —
such a person is spared toil in this world,
and his work is done by others,
כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי (בְּרָכוֹת לה, ב),
and the yoke of earning a living is removed from him.
וּמִי שֶׁלֹּא יָגַע בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
But one who did not toil in the Oral Torah,
"'and you will be sated' — this is drinking,"
the wine of the Oral Torah —
he toils and is not sated,
and only the nations of the world are sated.
And this is how he expounded "And your toil":
And the toil of most people
who fulfill the command of the Omnipresent
"And you shall gather in your grain," etc.,
"and you shall eat and be sated."
But one who is not worthy —
the nations of the world are sated.
And this is "for that which does not satisfy":
that you were not sated with the wine of Torah.
the yoke of the Oral Torah,
no toil at all would have been needed,
for one who does the will of the Omnipresent,
his work is done by others:
וְעָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, ה),
"Strangers shall stand and tend your flocks" (Yeshayahu 61:5),
and no toil at all is needed,
as it was before the corruption,
and as it will be in the future,
when "the Land of Israel is destined
and garments of fine wool," etc.
For toil in the Oral Torah
rescues from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
and as a result one is spared
the subjugation of the kingdoms as well,
for the one depends on the other:
because they have grounds for accusation,
in that something of their kelipah is found in Israel too,
and they are able to be sated, Heaven forbid,
But one who accepts upon himself
the yoke of the Oral Torah
is spared the leaven in the dough
and the subjugation of the kingdoms,
and he needs no toil at all,
for his work is done by others.
And in the Pesikta (ibid.) he also brings
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי כד, ד):
"And by knowledge are the chambers filled
with all precious and pleasant wealth."
"Pleasant things are at Your right hand forever,"
וְנִדְרָשׁ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֱמוֹר שָׁם; וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה ל, ב)
which is expounded (Midrash Rabbah, Emor, ibid.; Vayikra Rabbah 30:2)
מַאן נָצַח? מַאן דְּנָקֵט בָּאיָין בִּידֵיהּ.
who has won? The one holding the palm branch in his hand.
And this is the connection of the verse
to the verse "And you shall take for yourselves
which depend on the mazal of Atika Kadisha
and this is "rather than choice gold."
וְזֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And this alludes to the Oral Torah,
which comes from the dew of Atika:
"My word shall distill like the dew" (Devarim 32:2),
with which to revive the dead;
and this is "the dew of Torah revives him"
And knowledge is the inwardness of Keser Elyon,
and this is the fiftieth gate
that was revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his companions.
